identification.summary: UNC4191 is a Mandiant uncategorized cluster that Mandiant assesses has a China nexus. Mandiant Managed Defense found it threat hunting and described espionage activity that relies heavily on USB devices for initial infection and concentrates on the Philippines [S1]. Victims were public and private sector entities primarily in Southeast Asia, extending to the US, Europe and Asia Pacific Japan (APJ) [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Mandiant: the campaign potentially extends back to September 2021, based on malware compile timestamps (1 and 9 September 2021). Mandiant cautions it may have detected only the later stages of the malware's proliferation [S1]. Press coverage differs on the start date [S3].
identification.notes: UNC4191 is a Mandiant cluster designation, not a named APT. No Microsoft name or MITRE group ID is established in the sources gathered. Mandiant did not tie it to a named group in its report [S1]. Check Point's 2023 Camaro Dragon USB reporting is similar in technique, but none of the sources gathered state that Camaro Dragon and UNC4191 are the same actor [S4][S5].

attribution.confidence: Mandiant states: "we assess it has a China nexus" [S1]. Mandiant did not attribute the activity to a specific state organization in the report [S1].
attribution.basis: Mandiant assessed the activity as supporting Chinese operations to gain and maintain access for intelligence collection related to China's political and commercial interests. It cited the targeting pattern, which it tied to regional geopolitical concerns [S1][S2]. A PDB path in MISTCLOAK contains Chinese characters meaning "disk hijacking" [S1].

objectives: Mandiant assesses the activity aims to gain and maintain access to public and private entities for intelligence collection related to China's political and commercial interests [S1]. DARKDEW is designed to copy files from removable drives, which could include data from air-gapped systems [S1].

regions: Philippines (main target by number of affected systems) [S1]
United States, Europe and APJ (organizations; systems still physically in the Philippines) [S1]
targeting.notes: Mandiant reports that even when the targeted organizations were based elsewhere, the targeted systems were physically located in the Philippines [S1]. The report does not name specific victim organizations or industry verticals beyond public and private sector [S1].

capabilities.summary: Initial access is physical: a user plugs in a compromised USB drive and runs a renamed, legitimately signed binary (T1091) [S1]. Renamed USB Network Gate binaries named "Removable Disk.exe" or "USB Drive.exe" side-load the MISTCLOAK launcher (u2ec.dll), which decrypts and runs an encrypted payload (usb.ini) [S1]. That payload is DARKDEW, a dropper and worm. It persists via a Run key, polls for removable drives every 10 seconds, and copies its files into a hidden autorun.inf folder on each new drive, enabling self-replication and transfer of collected files [S1]. BLUEHAZE, using a renamed legitimate Razer binary (DateCheck.exe) to side-load a malicious DLL, runs a renamed NCAT (wuwebv.exe) to open a reverse shell to closed[.]theworkpc[.]com on port 80 [S1]. Mandiant saw no evidence of reverse shell interaction and noted visibility gaps or short log retention might explain this [S1]. Mandiant published YARA rules and detection ideas, including processes launched from non-C: drive roots and filename/OriginalFileName mismatches [S1].

campaigns.name: Earliest malware compile timestamps
campaigns.summary: MISTCLOAK, DARKDEW and BLUEHAZE samples carry compile timestamps of 1 September 2021 and 9 September 2021, and Mandiant says the campaign potentially extends back to September 2021 [S1].

campaigns.name: Mandiant publishes UNC4191 findings
campaigns.summary: Mandiant Managed Defense reports a USB-borne, Philippines-focused China-nexus espionage campaign using MISTCLOAK, DARKDEW, BLUEHAZE and NCAT, and states it will continue to monitor the cluster [S1][S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Related USB-spreading activity reported by Check Point (Camaro Dragon)
campaigns.summary: Check Point reports a separate USB-spreading campaign it attributes to Camaro Dragon (HopperTick launcher, WispRider payload), which it links to Mustang Panda and LuminousMoth. This is a different vendor cluster and is not stated to be UNC4191 [S4][S5].

diamond.adversary: China-nexus cluster tracked by Mandiant as UNC4191; no named group or state organization is identified [S1].
diamond.capability: USB-borne worm chain of MISTCLOAK, DARKDEW and BLUEHAZE, DLL side-loading of signed binaries, and a renamed NCAT reverse shell [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: NCAT reverse shell C2 at closed[.]theworkpc[.]com:80; staging directories C:\ProgramData\udisk and C:\Users\Public\Libraries\CNNUDTV [S1]. Physical removable media is the primary delivery vehicle [S1].
diamond.victim: Public and private entities, primarily in Southeast Asia and especially the Philippines, with some in the US, Europe and APJ [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Mandiant assesses the activity supports collection tied to China's political and commercial interests, with regional geopolitical interests as context for the Philippines focus [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Windows hosts with removable media enabled and unrestricted execution of signed binaries from USB roots; potentially air-gapped systems reachable by USB [S1].

gaps: Mandiant's original report is the only primary technical source; no later Mandiant/Google update on UNC4191 was found in the searches run.
No named group, sponsor, or government attribution is established; Mandiant gives only a 'China nexus' assessment [S1].

Relationship to Camaro Dragon / Mustang Panda / LuminousMoth is not established in the sources gathered; one search summary mentioned a Trend Micro link to Mustang Panda, but I could not verify that claim, so it is not included.
Specific victim organizations, sectors, and data actually exfiltrated are not public; Mandiant saw no reverse shell interaction [S1].
Start date: Mandiant's compile timestamps indicate September 2021, while some press coverage cites April 2022; not reconciled [S1][S3].
Hash labels in the IOC table of the Mandiant report may not align cleanly with body text; verify against sample metadata before use.
Could not open The Record, Industrial Cyber, ETDA, or Hacker News pages directly (host unreachable); Hacker News is cited from search-result summaries only.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is removable media and the personnel who handle it, especially at sites in or near the Philippines, since Mandiant found targeted systems physically located there even for organizations based elsewhere [S1]. Air-gapped or isolated enclaves are in scope because DARKDEW copies files to and from removable drives [S1]. STEP 2: The adversary operates through physical media and low-cost, legitimately signed binaries, which bypasses network perimeter defenses [S1]. STEP 3: The template is a USB with a renamed signed binary, then DLL side-loading (MISTCLOAK), then DARKDEW dropper and worm propagation, then a BLUEHAZE/NCAT reverse shell [S1]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued USB-borne collection against Southeast Asian public and private entities, including partner-nation and US-affiliated sites in the region. MDCOA is a worm-propagated infection crossing into air-gapped or classified-adjacent enclaves through shared removable media at conferences or exercises, with the reverse shell used to pull data. Candidate indicators: processes launched from non-C: drive roots, hidden autorun.inf\Protection for Autorun folders, C:\ProgramData\udisk, Run-key values 'udisk' or 'ACNTV', renamed binaries whose OriginalFileName mismatches, and DNS to closed[.]theworkpc[.]com [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: removable-media events and the Mandiant-published detections should feed theater cyber SA for Indo-Pacific mission partners [S1]. (2) Authorities: removable-media controls and the right to scan or quarantine personal and partner media on mission networks need to be confirmed with the owning commander and network owner before incident response. (3) Mission assurance: air-gapped or isolated enclaves are not protected by isolation alone, so media-handling policy and data-transfer procedures are mission assurance items [S1]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partner nations in Southeast Asia through established channels, since the Philippines is the main target [S1]. Treat attribution beyond 'China nexus' as unestablished when briefing [S1].

provenance.importedSummary: UNC4191 is a China-linked threat actor that has been involved in cyber espionage campaigns targeting public and private sectors primarily in Southeast Asia. They have been known to use USB devices as an initial infection vector and have been observed deploying various malware families on infected systems. UNC4191's operations have also extended to the US, Europe, and the Asia Pacific Japan region, with a particular focus on the Philippines.
